questions.question: Following an order of 16 July 2021 , the Supreme Court of India introduced an electronic system named ________, in November 2021, through which its crucial decisions can be communicated electronically to prison authorities and investigating agencies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**FASTER.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** introduced an **electronic system **in **November 2021** to communicate its crucial decisions **electronically** to **prison authorities** and investigating agencies.
 
• The system is named **FASTER**, which stands for **"Fast and Secure Transmission of Electronic Records."**
 
• This system is expected to expedite the process of delivering the court's orders to** prison authorities and investigating agencies, **reducing the time taken for **manual processing **and **physical delivery** of the orders.
 
• With this system, the court aims to ensure that the orders are **communicated quickly **and securely to the concerned authorities, thereby **reducing delays** in the justice delivery system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Supreme Court of India** is the** highest court** in the Republic of India and the ultimate **judicial authority.**
 
• The **Chief Justice of India** and up to **33 more justices** make up the Supreme Court.
 
• Through its** original, appellate, and advisory **authorities, it possesses a wide range of powers.
 
• **DY Chandrachud **is the Chief Justice of India at the moment.

questions.question: Select the correct statement from the given options.

options.text: There is very little temperature difference between day and night in the coastal areas of Kerala.
There is very little temperature difference between day and night in Rajasthan.
There is extreme cold in southern India during winter season.
There is plenty of rain observed in central India throughout the year.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**There is very little temperature difference between day and night in the coastal areas of Kerala.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala** is a state located in the southern part of India, and it is known for its **coastal areas.**
 
• Due to the** proximity of the sea,** the coastal areas of Kerala experience a **moderate climate **with** very little temperature difference **between day and night.
 
• The temperature in Kerala's coastal areas ranges from **20oC to 30oC** throughout the year, making it a popular tourist destination.
 
• The coastal areas of Kerala also receive** heavy rainfall** during the monsoon season, which lasts from** June to September.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajasthan** is a **desert state** located in the **northern part of India** and experiences** extreme temperatures** during summer and winter seasons.
 
• **Central India** is a **semi-arid region** with a **monsoon climate**, and rainfall is limited to the monsoon season.
 
• **India's climate** is characterized by a broad spectrum of weather patterns.
 
 
• According to the **Köppen system**, India has **six main climatic subtypes**: the west has **arid deserts**, the north has **alpine tundra and glaciers,** and the southwest and **island territories** have wet tropical regions that support rain forests.
 
• India's topography and geology play a key role in its climate; the** Himalayas in the north **and the **Thar Desert **in the** northwest **combine to produce a **monsoonal regime** that is significant to **both culture **and the country's economy.
 
• The majority of India can be considered** tropical in climate,** even though the **Tropic of Cancer, **the line between the** tropics and subtropics,** crosses through the center of the nation.

questions.question: By what name did Allauddin Khilji build his capital?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Siri.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** capital city** that **Allauddin Khilji** built was called **Siri.**
 
• It was located near the present-day village of **Shahpur Jat in Delhi** and served as the political and cultural center of the** Delhi Sultanate** during his reign.
 
• Some of the **notable features **of Siri were:
 
 
• A **massive fortification system** that included **walls, gates, and bastions** to protect the city from external threats.
 
• A **grand palace complex** that housed the royal court, administrative offices, and living quarters for the sultan and his family.
 
• A **central market or bazaar** that attracted merchants and traders from different parts of the world.
 
• Several **mosques, madrasas, and public buildings** that reflected the **Islamic architectural style** and **religious ethos** of the time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dinpanah** was a city founded by the **Mughal emperor Humayun **in the mid-16th century, long after the reign of Allauddin Khilji.

 
 
• It was located near the present-day **Purana Qila in Delhi **and served as a **refuge for Humayun** during his exile from India. 
 
 
 
• **Allauddin Khilji** was a prominent ruler of the** Khilji Dynasty **who ruled over the **Delhi Sultanate** from **1296 to 1316 CE**.
 
 
• He is known for his **military campaigns** and **administrative reforms**, as well as his patronage of **art and literature.**

questions.question: The policy of dual system of government of Bengal was the brainchild of which of these?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Clive.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **dual system** of government of** Bengal** was introduced in **1765 by Lord Clive**, who was the Governor-General of India at that time.
 
• The policy was implemented after the** Battle of Plassey in 1757**, which gave the British East India Company control over Bengal, one of the richest provinces in India.
 
• Under the dual system of government, the British East India Company became the** de facto ruler of Bengal, **while the **Nawab of Bengal **remained the** titular head** of the province.
 
• The policy was aimed at ensuring that the British East India Company could **exploit **the resources of Bengal without having to bear the responsibilities of governance.
 
• The dual system of government continued until the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, after which the British Crown took over the governance of India from the East India Company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Hastings** was the Governor-General of Bengal from **1813 to 1823**.

 
 
• He is known for his administrative reforms, including the establishment of the** Indian Civil Service **and the introduction of **English education** in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Lytton** was the Viceroy of India from **1876 to 1880**.
 
 
• He is known for his controversial policies, including the **Vernacular Press Act,** which curbed the freedom of the press in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie** was the Governor-General of India from **1848 to 1856.**
 
 
• He is known for his reforms, including the introduction of the** Doctrine of Lapse, **which allowed the British to annex Indian states that did not have a male heir.

questions.question: Identify the ODD one out.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**White revolution.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Modern agricultural** technology, **Green revolution,** and **Seed-fertiliser-water** technology are all related to **increasing agricultural productivity** and efficiency, while **White revolution** is related to the** increase in milk production** in India.
 
• **Green revolution **refers to the use of **high-yielding varieties** of **crops,** **improved irrigation**, and **modern agricultural techniques** to increase crop productivity.
 
 
• It was introduced in India in the 1960s and led to a **significant increase** in food production.
 
 
 
• **Seed-fertiliser-water technology** is a modern agricultural technique that involves using **high-quality seeds**, **appropriate fertilizers,** and **efficient irrigation methods** to increase crop yields.
 
• **Modern agricultural technology** encompasses a wide range of techniques and methods, including** precision farming, biotechnology, and mechanization**, among others.
 
• These techniques aim to improve **agricultural efficiency and reduce costs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **White revolution**, also known as **Operation Flood,** was a **dairy development program** launched in India in **1970.**
 
• It aimed to increase milk production and make India** self-sufficient** in milk production.
 
• The program was successful in increasing milk production and creating a **cooperative network** of milk producers in India.
 
• It led to the establishment of **Amul, a dairy cooperative** that has become a household name in India.
 
• The success of the White revolution was due to the efforts of **Dr. Verghese Kurien**, who is often referred to as the **father of the White revolution** in India.
 
• The program involved the introduction of modern dairy farming techniques, such as** artificial insemination** and improved **cattle feed.**
 
• It also involved the establishment of **milk collection centers** and **processing plants,** which helped to increase the market for milk and dairy products.

questions.question: In which period is the first inscriptional example of the practice of Sati found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gupta.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** first inscriptional **example of the **practice of Sati **is found in the **Gupta period.**
 
• **Sati** was a practice where a **widow **would immolate herself on her** husband's funeral pyre.**
 
• The **Gupta period** was known for its cultural and artistic achievements, as well as its **promotion of Hinduism.**
 
• The **Maukhari and Vardhana dynasties** were both North Indian dynasties that preceded the Gupta dynasty.
 
• The** Satavahana dynasty** was a South Indian dynasty that existed before the Gupta period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Evangelists like **Carey** and Hindu reformers like **Ram Mohan Roy **opposed the practice of sati, which finally prompted British Governor-General of India **Lord William Bentinck** to implement the** Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829.**
 
• It stated that Hindu widows who are **burned or buried alive** will face legal action from the **criminal courts.**
 
• Subsequent laws were passed to combat what the British believed to be connected problems concerning** violence against Hindu women**.
 
• These laws included the **Age of Consent Act of 1891,** the **Female Infanticide Prevention Act of 1870**, and the** Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act of 1856.**
 
• Sati is defined as the **act or rite **itself in **Part I, Section 2(c) **of the Indian Commission of **Sati (Prevention) Act, 1987**.

questions.question:
Choose the correct set of the names for the organic compounds in the given figure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/74a908762ead42e33992df5ade2872edd931fbeeac36dcc1473813b2274a95d3.png]

options.text: a: Furan, b: Toluene, c: Pyridine
a: Furan, b: Pyridine, c: Thiophene
a: Furan, b: Thiophene, c: Aniline

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Furan **is a **heterocyclic organic compound** containing a **five-membered aromatic ring** with **one oxygen **atom.
 
• **Toluene** is a **colorless liquid **with a **sweet, pungent odor**.
 
 
• It is a **common solvent **and used as a precursor to many chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Pyridine** is a** heterocyclic aromatic compound** with a **six-membered ring** containing **five carbon atoms** and **one nitrogen atom.**
 
 
• It is used as a **solvent, catalyst, and precursor **to many chemicals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thiophene** is a** heterocyclic compound **containing a **five-membered aromatic ring **with **one sulfur **atom.

 
 
• It is used as a **solvent **and in the production of **pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals.**
 
 
 
• **Aniline** is an **aromatic amine** with a **benzene ring** and a primary **amine group**.
 
 
• It is used in the production of **dyes, pharmaceuticals, and rubber processing chemicals.**
 
 
 
• **Anisole** is an organic compound with a **methoxy group (-OCH3)** attached to a benzene ring.
 
 
• It is used as a** solvent** and in the production of **perfumes and flavors.**

questions.question: Which state ranked first among the 18 large and mid-sized states (with population of over one crore each) in justice delivery in India as per the second edition of the India Justice Report?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The** India Justice Report** is a **comprehensive study** that evaluates the performance of the country's** justice delivery system** across various parameters, including **infrastructure, human resources, diversity, budgets, workload, and outcomes.**
 
• The** second edition** of the report, released in **November 2020, **covered** 18 large** and** mid-sized states** that account for about** 90%** of the country's population and **95% **of its pending cases.
 
• **Maharashtra** ranked **first** among these states with an overall score of** 4.4 out of 5**, followed by **Tamil Nadu (4.2), Telangana (4.1), Punjab (4.0), and Kerala (3.9).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Maharashtra **performed **well** in most of the sub-categories, such as** infrastructure, diversity, and budget utilization**.
 
 
• But it lagged behind in the parameter of **clearance rate**, which measures the percentage of cases disposed of against the number of cases instituted in a year.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu, **which ranked second, scored **high **in the parameters of diversity, case management, and disposal rate.
 
 
• But it faced challenges in the areas of **budget utilization** and **human resources.**

questions.question: What is the duty of the Chief Minister, as mentioned under Article 167 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
Appointment and removal of Council of the Ministers.
Appointment of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
Appointment of Advocate General of the state in consultation with Attorney general.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 167 **of the Indian Constitution deals with the **duties of the Chief Minister**.
 
• It states that it shall be the duty of the Chief Minister to communicate to the **Governor **of the State all decisions of the **Council of Ministers** relating to the administration of the affairs of the** State and proposals for legislation**. 
 
• This duty is important as it ensures that the Governor is **kept informed** of the decisions taken by the Council of Ministers, who are responsible for the **governance** of the State.
 
• The communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor helps in maintaining** transparency and accountability** in the functioning of the State Government.
 
• It also helps in ensuring that the Governor is able to exercise his/her **constitutional powers and functions** effectively, such as giving assent to** Bills passed** by the State Legislature or **summoning and proroguing** the Legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Chief Minister **is responsible for the **selection of the Council of Ministers**, who are collectively responsible to the State Legislature.

 
 
• The Chief Minister can **recommend the removal of a Minister **to the Governor, but the final decision lies with the Governor.
 
 
 
• The **Speaker** is elected by the **members of the Legislative Assembly **from among themselves and is not appointed by the Chief Minister.
 
• The **Advocate General **is appointed by the** Governor **in consultation with the** Chief Minister **and holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.

questions.question: Which water-soluble pigment belonging to a phenolic group is present in pomegranate, eggplant, black carrots and red cabbage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anthocyanins.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anthocyanins** is a **water-soluble pigment **that is present in** pomegranate, eggplant, black carrots, and red cabbage.**
 
• It belongs to a **phenolic group.**
 
• These are responsible for the **red, purple, and blue **colors in many fruits, vegetables, and flowers. 
 
• They have **antioxidant and anti-inflammatory** properties and are being studied for their potential health benefits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phycoerythrin **is a water-soluble pigment found in **red algae and cyanobacteria.**

 
 
• It is used in **biotechnology** as a** fluorescent label **and in medical research as a **diagnostic tool.**
 
 
 
• **Phycobilins **are water-soluble pigments found in **cyanobacteria and some red algae.**
 
 
• They are involved in** photosynthesis** and act as **accessory pigments** that capture light energy.
 
 
 
• **Betalains** are water-soluble pigments found in** beets and cacti.**
 
 
• They are responsible for the** red and yellow colors** in these plants and have **antioxidant **properties.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits religious instructions in any statefunded educational institution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 28.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 28** of the Indian Constitution **prohibits religious instructions **in any state-funded educational institution. 
 
• Article 28 falls under **Part III **of the Indian Constitution, which deals with **fundamental rights.**
 
• It specifically deals with the **right to freedom of religion**.
 
• Clause (1) of Article 28 states that no religious instruction shall be provided in any **educational institution** wholly maintained out of state funds.
 
• This means that any school or college that **receives funding** from the government **cannot impart **religious teachings to its students.
 
• However, Clause (2) of Article 28 allows for religious instruction to be provided in educational institutions that are **administered by the state** but not wholly maintained out of state funds.
 
• In such cases, attendance in such classes must be **voluntary **for students.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It is important to note tha**t Article 28 **only applies to institutions that are** funded or administered by the state**.
 
• **Private institutions** are not bound by this provision.
 
• **Article 29** deals with the **protection of interests of minorities** in educational institutions.
 
• **Article 30 **deals with the** right of minorities** to establish and administer **educational institutions.**
 
• **Article 27** Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion

questions.question: Which of the followings is NOT an example of factor payment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pension.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Factor payment** refers to payments made to **factors of production,** which are the resources used in the **production of goods and services.**
 
• These factors include **land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship.**
 
• **Interest, wages, rent,** are all examples of factor payments.
 
• Interest is paid to **capital**, wages are paid to **labor**, rent is paid to** land**, and pension is paid to** retired labor.**
 
• However, pension is **not a** factor payment as it is paid to retired labor and **not to active labor.**
 
• Factor payment is made to the factors of production that are **actively involved** in the production process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interest** is the payment made for the use of** borrowed capital.**
 
• **Wages** are the payment made to** labor for their services.**
 
• **Rent **is the payment made for the **use of land** and other** natural resources.**
 
• The most widely utilized factor in **macroeconomic analysis** is factor income, which aids governments in identifying the distinction between **GDP and GNP.**
 
• It can also be used to highlight discrepancies in the **allocation of revenue.**

questions.question: Which is the largest container port in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru Port.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru Port** is located in the state of **Maharashtra** and is the** largest container port** in India.
 
• It handles over** 50% of India's container traffic** and is a crucial hub for **trade** in the country.
 
• The port is also known for its **state-of-the-art facilities **and **efficient operations.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kandla Port** is located in the state of **Gujarat **and is one of the major ports in India.

 
 
• It primarily handles **dry cargo **such as** salt, iron ore, and textiles.**
 
 
 
• **Kolkata Port** is located in the state of** West Bengal **and is one of the oldest ports in India.
 
 
• It primarily handles** bulk cargo **such as **coal, iron ore, and petroleum** products.
 
 
 
• **Hazira Port** is located in the state of **Gujarat **and is a relatively new port, having started operations in **2005.**
 
 
• It primarily handles **liquid cargo **such as** crude oil and petroleum** products.

questions.question: Which physical unit is defined as the field intensity that produces one newton (N) of force per ampere (A) per meter of conductor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tesla.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The physical unit defined as producing** one Newton (N) of force per meter per ampere (A)** of current flowing through it is known as** Tesla.**
 
• The derived **SI unit** of **magnetic flux density**, or the strength of a magnetic field, is the tesla (T).
 
• **One Weber per square meter** is represented by one Tesla.
 
• The **gauss** is the analogous and **obsolete cgs unit**. 
 
• There are precisely **10,000 gauss** in one Tesla.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kelvin** is the unit of **temperature.**
 
• **Coulomb** is the unit of **electric charge**.
 
• **Pascal** is the unit of **pressure.**
 
• **Ampere** is the unit of **electric current.**
